newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Zealand says no progress in Burma charter.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand says no progress in Burma charter.

text.p: New Zealand's foreign and trade minister Don McKinnon said on Wednesday Burma's military government had made no progress in drafting a new constitution, a Thai government spokesman said.
McKinnon also suggested during talks with Thai premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh at government house that Rangoon set a time frame to complete the charter, the spokesman said.

"The New Zealand foreign and trade minister told ... (Chavalit) that Burma has made no progress in its drafting of the constitution and suggested that if Rangoon wanted to gain recognition from the international community, they should set a clear agenda and time frame for such matters," the spokesman said in a statement.

A National Convention has been meeting intermittently since 1993 to draft guidelines for the new constitution. The convention of mostly hand-picked delegates was due to resume late last year but has remained idle for about a year.

Burmese opposition leader and Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi withdrew her National League for Democracy (NLD) party from the convention in November 1995, saying it was not democratic and did not represent the will of the people.
One of the main guidelines of the new charter, which still some way from completion, is that the military will continue to have a strong say and role in future government.

Chavalit told McKinnon that officials in Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) told him the drafting of the constitution had reach a crucial point, the statement said. It did not elaborate.
McKinnon was on an official visit to Thailand.
Burma was accepted as a full member of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) at a meeting of the group in Malaysia last week.

Its induction into the group came despite protests from many Western nations which said acceptance would be tantamount to approval of the SLORC's widespread human rights abuses and its failure to recognise the democracy movement.
The NLD won a landslide victory in a 1990 election but the result was never recognised by the SLORC.
